nodes.summary: Writing $\varphi_c$ for the partial function on $\mathbb{N}$ computed by a code $c$ of a partial recursive function, the set of codes $c$ with $\varphi_c(0)$ defined is many-one reducible to the set of total codes, the codes that halt on every input: there is a computable function $f$ from codes to codes such that, for every code $c$, $\varphi_c(0)$ is defined if and only if $f(c)$ is total.
nodes.title: Halting on zero reduces to totality

nodes.summary: Writing $\varphi_c$ for the partial function on $\mathbb{N}$ computed by a code $c$ of a partial recursive function, the set of codes $c$ with $\varphi_c(0)$ undefined is many-one reducible to the set of total codes, the codes that halt on every input: there is a computable function $f$ from codes to codes such that, for every code $c$, $\varphi_c(0)$ is undefined if and only if $f(c)$ is total.
nodes.title: Non-halting on zero reduces to totality

nodes.summary: The set of total codes, the codes of partial recursive functions that halt on every input, is not co-recognizable by multi-stack machines: no multi-stack machine halts on the binary encoding of a code $c$ exactly when $c$ is not total.
nodes.title: Totality is not co-recognizable

nodes.summary: The set of total codes, the codes of partial recursive functions that halt on every input, is not decidable by multi-stack machines: no multi-stack machine computes a total function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ that takes the value $1$ at the number encoding a code $c$ exactly when $c$ is total.
nodes.title: Totality is undecidable

nodes.summary: The set of total codes, the codes of partial recursive functions that halt on every input, is not recognizable by multi-stack machines: no multi-stack machine halts on the binary encoding of a code $c$ exactly when $c$ is total.
nodes.title: Totality is not recognizable

nodes.summary: A code $c$ of a partial recursive function is total when it halts on every input: writing $\varphi_c$ for the partial function on $\mathbb{N}$ that $c$ computes, $\varphi_c(n)$ is defined for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Total codes

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ of a partial recursive function, this is the partial function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ that on input $k$ is undefined if $c$ halts on input $0$ within $k$ steps of bounded evaluation, and equals $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Diverging once a code halts on zero

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
